# Implicit Chain-of-Thought

> A reading list about reasoning without writing every intermediate step, with explanations, paper summaries, and downloadable citations.

## Using the data

Use the original papers for scientific claims. Summaries and categories are written for this reading list, not copied abstracts. Papers can belong to several categories. Coverage includes related generation methods and is not exhaustive.

- `id` identifies a paper; `paper_url` links to the original source; `record_url` links to its entry on this site.
- `author_names` preserves the authors' names and order.
- `first_public` is the earliest public date we have verified, usually the first arXiv submission. An earlier conference presentation has a source note. It is not an independently verified announcement date.
- `citation_date` is the initial submission date of the linked arXiv preprint. BibTeX and CSL-JSON describe that preprint, not a later proceedings version. Source URLs may serve revised versions.
- `provenance` says where we first found a paper.
- Category IDs and filter values are defined in the category file; related terms are not necessarily synonyms.
